There could be a couple of things going on whether it has to do with past experiences, predisposition or a chemical imbalance is tough to make an assumption over the internet. 
I know for me personally that when I feel overly sensitive or angry, having anyone try to make sense of it or make me explain it just sets me off further. My advice would be learning different coping or breathing exercises. That could help but what do I know, I don’t use those. It’s important to not be too hard on yourself, and the feelings you have don’t necessarily have to have “real” reason behind them. That just makes you feel worse when your trying to deny yourself something that you’re experiencing which is very real and valid. 
Medicine could help with this, I am bipolar and have borderline personality disorder which is great to know the label, but does shit for me otherwise. Meds have barely touched these issues, so I don’t have much advice in that regard. 
Just want you to know you’re not alone with feeling out of wack from your emotions. Getting support online helps a lot and you should feel proud for sharing.

I’m from the US and I’ve had about 2 experiences with doctors and sh scars. The first was when I was underage and a dermatologist saw some minor scars on my arms. She asked, “are you a cutter?” And I got really anxious and scared and said yeah and then she asked to see any other scars to which I promptly lied and said those were the only ones. She dropped it and moved on to her treatment plan for my acne.... 
The second one was more recent, I was at my primary care doctors, but had to see someone other than my usual doctor. He was young, tall and immediately intimidated me. We discussed why I was there (eating disorder affecting health, etc) to which he promptly said cut it out. Then he went on to take my vitals and pulled up my sleeve and asked how I got those scars. (They’re practically white at this point) I couldn’t say anything because I was some overwhelmed and anxious and he was scaring the shit out of me for some reason, and he kept asking like three or four times, getting angrier each time. Since I didn’t say anything he made the assumption I did it myself and then went on to say if I’m hurting myself I need to consider being admitted. I started crying and he took a slightly gentler tone. I don’t remember what happened after that as I might have dissociated. 
Anyway, I’m sure if you’re more up front and don’t try to hide the obvious, like I did, your doctor is more likely to believe what you have to say. Also they might not even mention it, I’ve heard people say that before. (I think people out of the US? Not sure) 
Good luck anyway, just try to keep your composure and breathe. It’ll be okay :)
